Chess for two to four players, with dice, bosses and a forge.

Two ways to play

Start with the classic board, or let the world turn against everyone at the table.

Game of Anchanets

Two players: two full armies of 16 pieces and no dice, pure strategy. Three or four players: corner armies of 8 pieces where two dice decide your actions each turn. With four, you play 2 against 2.

A little hellish twist

Turn on board events like Gravity Instability, Blood Moon and Landslide. Each one changes the rules for a few days, and the game shows how many days are left.

Craft it. Equip it.

Gear is part of every piece. Make it at the forge, then decide who carries it.

Crafter

Place resources around the forge core and craft items such as the Scale Cloak, Shattered Whip and Ancient Core. Normal, Fused and Smithing circuits give you more ways to build.

Armory

Tap a piece to open its storage. One item per piece, up to 8 equipped. Pick how equipment looks on the board, from a full look to a ring with a faint picture.

Fight the Titans

Every boss has a health bar and an army of its own. Bring your best-equipped pieces.

  • Ruler of Hollow surrounds itself with a ring of skeletons in the middle of the board.
  • Devourer of Worlds waits at the centre while your army marches to it.
  • Each boss has its own background, so you always know who you face.

Survive the Nightmare

Apocalypse Nightmare never ends. Zombie waves keep coming, and you hold the line for as long as you can.

  • A live counter shows your time, the wave size and the zombie count.
  • Your best five runs are saved on the leaderboard.

About the game
चतुरङ्ग

The game behind I.O.N

I.O.N is built on Chaturanga, which means “four limbs of an army”. It began in India about 1,500 years ago and is the ancestor of chess. Here is how the game works, taken from the Records books inside the app.

Pick your game

Choose the number of players on the start screen, then tap Start.

2 players
Two full armies of 16 pieces. No dice, pure strategy. Player 1 starts, and you must move: you cannot pass.
3 or 4 players
Small armies of 8 pieces in the corners. Two dice decide which pieces may move. Turns go clockwise from Player 1 at the bottom left.
Teams of 2
In a 4 player game, opposite corners are allies: Player 1 with 3, and Player 2 with 4. Allies cannot capture each other.
Moving a piece. Tap one of your pieces and its squares light up. A dot is an empty square, and a ring means you can capture there. Tap a coloured square to move. A captured piece is removed for good, and you can never land on your own piece.

The pieces

The 2 player game uses the six classic Chaturanga pieces.

Rajaking
Moves 1 square in any direction. It can never step onto a square an enemy could capture. Lose it and you lose the game.
Mantricounselor
Moves 1 square diagonally. A weak helper that always stays on the same colour of square.
Gajaelephant
Jumps exactly 2 squares diagonally and hops over anything. It never moves 1 square, so each Gaja can only ever reach 8 squares.
Ashvahorse
Moves in an L: 2 squares straight, then 1 sideways. It jumps over pieces.
Rathachariot
Slides any distance up, down, left or right, and stops at the first piece in its way. The strongest piece.
Padatifoot soldier
Moves 1 square forward onto an empty square. Captures 1 square straight or diagonally forward. No double step. At the far end it becomes a Mantri.
3 and 4 players use different pieces: Hasti (elephant) slides like the Ratha, and Nau (boat) jumps 2 squares diagonally like the Gaja. There is no Mantri, Ratha or Gaja in that game. Not in I.O.N: queen, castling, en passant, double pawn step and bishops.

How a 2 player game ends

Check
Your Raja is under attack and you must fix it. Moves that leave your own Raja attacked are never shown.
Checkmate
Your Raja is in check and nothing can save it. You lose.
Stalemate
You are not in check but have no legal move. The player who caused it wins, which is the old shatranj rule.
Bare king
Capture every enemy piece except the Raja and you win. It is a draw if the enemy can do the same to you on the very next move.

The dice game

On your turn, tap Roll dice. Each die is one play: move one matching piece. You may use the same piece twice, or skip a play. If no matching piece can move, that play is lost. Glowing pieces are the ones your dice allow.

1 or 5Raja or Padati
2Nau (boat)
3Ashva (horse)
4 or 6Hasti (elephant)

Points and winning

Each capture scores points: Padati 1, Nau 2, Ashva 3, Hasti 4, Raja 5. There is no check in this game, so a Raja is simply captured like any other piece, and that player is out. The game ends when only one player or one team is left, and the highest score wins. In a 4 player game the team totals count.

House rule. The old rules give no bonus roll for doubles. If you want one, turn on “Roll again on doubles” in Settings.

Elemental Madness

A custom mode for the 3 or 4 player dice game. Open it from Custom on the start screen. One day is one full round, and random events strike the board. The longer it stays calm, the likelier the next one. A banner shows when an event starts and ends, and you can tap the bar under the board to see what it does.

Storm
Once: every piece moves 1 square forward, back, left or right if a square is free.
Wind Gust
Once: each piece has a 50% chance to be pushed 1 square in a random direction.
Earthquake
2 days: Hasti and Ashva cannot move, even if the dice allow them.
Tsunami
Once: each player’s boats and 2 random pawns jump to random free squares.
Snow
2 days: one of your dice freezes each turn, so you get only 1 play.
Heatwave
2 days: the dice show pawn, king and boat faces 30% more often.
Gravity Instability
2 days: a random square becomes a gravity point that pulls nearby pieces toward it each day.
Eclipse
3 days: every pawn is too scared to move. The screen tints grey.
Blood Moon
2 days: Hasti and Ashva dice come up 30% more often. The screen tints red.
Rare events
Elemental Fusion makes two events happen together. If Eclipse and Blood Moon meet, they merge into a Bloody Eclipse.

Titans

Everyone fights one boss together. Setup and movement come from the standard game, but there are no dice. 1 or 2 players get the full 16 piece army, and 3 or 4 players get the 8 piece corner army.

Your turn
You have 2 move-points: move two pieces once each, or one piece twice. After everyone has gone, the boss acts.
Attacking
Move onto an enemy or any boss tile. Your piece stays put and deals the damage. The Raja deals 3 to a boss, a Padati deals 1, and other pieces deal 1 with a 10% chance to crit for 2.
Good to know
If your Raja falls, your army goes rogue. Lava is instant death. A feared piece can still move, but it costs your whole turn. Everyone still standing shares the win when the boss falls.

The bosses

Ancient Dread
A black dragon. It slams, turns open tiles into lava, and flies up to crash down on a marked square.
Avatar of Plague
A green hydra. Its Cultists guard it, and you must break them all before it appears.
King of Hollow
Rises from a crack in a field of bone with 12 Bone Knights.
Queen of Abomination
Starts as a cocoon. Destroy it and she hatches, stronger the longer it lived.
Empress of the Deep
Two bodies, the Empress and her Shadow, share one health bar.
Sovereign of Souls
A blazing golden bird sitting on a hoard of coins.
Devourer of Worlds
A world-eating giant that fills a 4 by 4 block of the board.
Practice first. The Training Dummy is a 20 hp target that never fights back. Hard Mode stays locked until you defeat all the Titans. Their stories are in the Titans History book.

Apocalypse Nightmare

1 player, in real time. There is no enemy army, just your pieces against a horde of zombies marching down from the north edge in growing waves. Capture them before they reach your ranks, because anyone they kill rises again as one of them. The board is 14 rows deep, and every minute the waves get nastier as another zombie type joins.

Your pieces learn new tricks

Recovery
A piece that attacks needs 1 second to recover before it can strike again, but it can still move freely. Ashva and Mantri never need to recover.
Padati
Free to roam: it can also step 1 square back, left or right, for moving only. A zombie within 2 squares makes it wind up a free strike.
Ratha and Gaja
They shrug off a zombie’s first hit and only turn into a zombie on the second.
Raja
Has 4 hit points and hits zombies for 2. Down to 1 hp, it rallies 3 fresh Padati once. If the Raja falls, every ability stops for the rest of that game.
What a fallen piece becomes. Raja becomes a Fallen Hero, Gaja a Tank, Ashva a Runner, and anything else a plain Zombie. The Endless Terror book lists every zombie that joins, from the first wave to the 40 minute mark.

Quick tips

Keep your Raja safe
In the 2 player game the Ratha is your strongest piece, so do not trade it cheaply.
Use the jumpers
Jumping pieces attack past blockers. Use them to reach pieces that look protected.
Stuck?
Tap a piece to see its moves. Nothing happens until you tap a coloured square.
